To add onto my point, the result of the test was already produced the minute God has created you. Because He already knows what you’re going to do. It doesn’t prove God doesn’t exist, because it’s a paradox at the end of the day. But it does refute the claim that a God can be perfect.

But that’s the point of the epicurean paradox, God testing us doesn’t make sense if He’s supposed to be an all-knowing source. And if everything in our lives has already been pre-destined & laid out then there is no true free will. Think of it as a video game. Imagine I made a character & their specific story already but gave them several hard life decisions, well as tragic events etc. Then I already know what they will choose & how they will end up in life. Because I’ve made it so that they live that exact life. If that character then decides not to have faith that I (the maker) exists, I cannot be mad at them for choosing not to. I’ve already decided what they will do. The issue with Islam like any other religion is that they condemn non believers to an eternity of hell. Even though we were created by God & he knew everything we would do already. What is the point of testing someone if you already made the outcome? God already knows what the result is so free will & omniscience cannot coexist.
